now that we have a species classification framework, We will test out a method for estimating volume based for the spatial tree list from `cloud2trees`:

We're going to attempt to use the [US National Scale Volume Biomass (NSVB) models](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104) to predict tree volume, biomass, and carbon. We'll implement code and functionality made available by Matthew Russell at [https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB](https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB).

since the files and code at [https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB](https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB) are not released as a package (and also include the requirement to set a working directory), we'll need to create a workflow to download the files and data, update the directories in the file that defines the functions, and then load the functions using `base::source()`. also, the `nsvb.R` file from that repository isn't entirely a collection of functions but a mix of function definitions and demonstrations, so we need to define the `tree` data used during some parts of that script

```{r}


# 1. Define the target directory and GitHub repository details
nsvb_dir_temp <- "../data/nsvb_files"

# if (!dir.exists(nsvb_dir_temp)) {
  dir.create(nsvb_dir_temp, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
  
  repo_temp <- "mbrussell/NSVB"
  # ?usethis::create_from_github
  
  usethis::create_from_github(
    repo_spec = repo_temp # "username/repositoryname"
    , destdir = nsvb_dir_temp
    , fork = F
    , open = F
    , rstudio = F
  )
  # Do you want to create anyway? .... For sure
  
  # utils::download.file(url = url_temp, destfile = zip_file_temp, mode = "wb", quiet = T)
  

  # nsvb.R has hardcoded paths... fix its internal working directory path
  script_dir_temp <- file.path(nsvb_dir_temp, "NSVB", "westfall gtr", "WO-GTR-104-Supp1")
  nsvb_f_temp  <- file.path(script_dir_temp, "nsvb.R")
  # if(file.exists(nsvb_f_temp)){
    lines_temp <- readLines(nsvb_f_temp, warn = FALSE)
    # lines_temp %>% head(n=11)
    
    # relative path
    rel_script_dir_temp <- normalizePath(script_dir_temp, winslash = "/", mustWork = T)
    # rel_script_dir_temp
    
    # columns in some nebulous "tree" dataframe
    tree_df_temp <- 
      paste0(
        "tree <- base::data.frame("
        , "EXAMPLE = base::numeric(0), "
        , "DIVISION = base::character(0), "
        , "PROVINCE = base::character(0), "
        , "STDORGCD = base::logical(0), "
        , "SPCD = base::numeric(0), "
        , "DIA = base::numeric(0), "
        , "HT = base::numeric(0), "
        , "ACTUALHT = base::numeric(0), "
        , "CR = base::numeric(0), "
        , "CULL = base::numeric(0), "
        , "DECAYCD = base::numeric(0), "
        , "STATUSCD = base::numeric(0), "
        , "Westfall_vol = base::numeric(0), "
        , "Westfall_bio = base::numeric(0), "
        , "Westfall_c = base::numeric(0)"
        , ")"
      )
    # tree_df_temp
    
    # add it
    lines_temp <- c(tree_df_temp, lines_temp)
    # lines_temp %>% head(n=11)
    
    # overwrite the hardcoded setwd() with our new local directory path
    updt_lines_temp <-
      stringr::str_replace(
        lines_temp
        , pattern     = "setwd.*" 
        , replacement = sprintf('setwd("%s")', rel_script_dir_temp) # safely enclose path
      )
    writeLines(updt_lines_temp, nsvb_f_temp)
  }else{
    stop(paste0("oops, can't find `",nsvb_f_temp,"` "))
  }

  # source it to load the functions
  source_script_wo_dir_change_fn <- function(file_path) {
    old_dir <- getwd()
    on.exit(setwd(old_dir)) # always restore initial working directory
    source(file = file_path)
  }
  
  source_script_wo_dir_change_fn(nsvb_f_temp)

# }
```

```{r}
library(allodb)
```

we'll start by using the FIA species code lookup table to get genus and species for all of our data sets based on the `species_symbol` (e.g. "PIPO", "POTR5", "QURU")

```{r}
# ref_trees_list
ref_trees_list <- 
  ref_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::map(
    \(df)
    df %>% 
      # get rid of columns we'll create
      dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
        , "genus"
        , "species"
        , "common_name"
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(
        fia_species_lookup %>% 
          dplyr::select(
            species_symbol
            , genus
            , species
            , common_name
          )
        , by = "species_symbol"
        , relationship = "many-to-one"
      )
  )
# pred_trees_list
pred_trees_list <- 
  pred_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::map(
    \(df)
    df %>% 
      # get rid of columns we'll create
      dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
        , "genus"
        , "species"
        , "common_name"
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(
        fia_species_lookup %>% 
          dplyr::select(
            species_symbol
            , genus
            , species
            , common_name
          )
        , by = "species_symbol"
        , relationship = "many-to-one"
      )
  )
```


let's take the `allodb::get_biomass()` function for a spin, demonstrating with the first study site: `r names(ref_trees_list)[1]`. 

required inputs for this function are: 

* `dbh`	- a numeric vector containing tree diameter at breast height (dbh) measurements, in cm.
* `genus` - a character vector (same length as dbh), containing the genus (e.g. "Quercus") of each tree.
* `coords` - a numeric vector of length 2 with longitude and latitude (if all trees were measured in the same location) or a matrix with 2 numerical columns giving the coordinates of each tree.
* `species` - a character vector (same length as dbh), containing the species (e.g. "rubra") of each tree. Default is NULL, when no species identification is available.

The function returns "A numeric vector of the same length as dbh, containing AGB value (in kg) for every stem."

this documentation is particularly interesting for noting that only `genus` is required and `species` is optional. based on the accuracy evaluation of the proposed classification method we just reviewed, we found that genus-level accuracy was generally higher, sometimes significantly higher, than species-level classification

```{r}
# ?allodb::get_biomass
ref_trees_list <- 
  ref_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::map(function(df){
    df$allodb_agb_kg <- allodb::get_biomass(
        dbh = df$dbh_cm
        , genus = df$genus
        , species = df$species
        , coords = 
          df %>%
            sf::st_transform(crs = sf::st_crs(4326)) %>%
            sf::st_coordinates() %>% 
            dplyr::as_tibble()
      )
    return(df)
  })

```

let's plot estimated total aboveground biomass (kg) versus DBH

```{r}
ref_trees_list[[1]] %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = dbh_cm, y = allodb_agb_kg, color = genus)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size=3, alpha=0.8) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(facets = dplyr::vars(genus)) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_d(option="turbo") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "DBH (cm)", y = "AGB (kg)") +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")

```
